correctness.rationale: For every integer n and every parameter the local normalized reciprocal-LCM factor is exactly a continuous power mean. Uniform O(1/p) log bounds combine with Pr(p|N)=1/p for O(sum_{p>P} p^-2) path-tail control and finite prime CRT convergence, proving the C([0,1]) limit. Independent geometric valuations construct the limit; all moments follow from uniform higher moment estimates. Full support follows from divergent positive local prime increments; Sperner anti-concentration of conditionally fair Bernoulli sums proves no atoms. The geometric series gives the kappa=2 exact mean. The standalone rational verifier replays exact local and convolution identities through n=200; no finite check is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source supplies extremal and averaged orders for a new Robin-normalized arithmetic family, leaving its behavior at a typical integer unexplained. The finding supplies the natural entire parameter process, complete marginal support and continuity (not just elementary mean asymptotics), a nontrivial antichain mechanism for eliminating atoms, a strict monotone coupling, and an exact special-parameter expectation; these are structurally informative and distinguish typical from extremal values.
